title: BitTorrent Ushers in Next-Gen Web3 Infrastructure with Strategic Rebrand and Inaugural BTT Burn
summary: The first round of BTT repurchased with decentralized service revenue has been completely burned, as BitTorrent leverages its reimagined architecture to pivot toward Web3 and AI infrastructure.    BitTorrent, a cornerstone of decentralized infrastructure in the TRON ecosystem, entered a new phase of...
content:
The first round of BTT repurchased with decentralized service revenue has been completely burned, as BitTorrent leverages its reimagined architecture to pivot toward Web3 and AI infrastructure. 

BitTorrent, a cornerstone of decentralized infrastructure in the TRON ecosystem, entered a new phase of growth driven by dual engines: the rollout of its long-term BTT buyback-and-burn strategy and a comprehensive brand upgrade.

Central to this strategic overhaul, the long-term BTT buyback-and-burn commitment has officially translated into tangible action. Following its announcement on July 6 and subsequent scheduled repurchases, BitTorrent transferred the first round of BTT—funded by 100% of decentralized service revenue—to a burn address on October 16, successfully completing its inaugural burn cycle. Coming on the heels of the recurring buyback-and-burn mechanisms established for JST and SUN, this marks another major positive development for the TRON ecosystem in deepening its token deflationary model and value accrual.

Concurrently, BitTorrent released a brand-new official whitepaper, marking a comprehensive brand upgrade. Directly answering the demands of the Web3 and generative AI era, this upgrade establishes a powerful tripartite architecture. It brings together the BitTorrent Mainnet for peer-to-peer content distribution, BTTInferGrid as the decentralized compute layer, and BTTC for cross-chain interoperability, Layer 2 scaling, and on-chain settlement. With the native BTT token serving as the unified economic engine across the entire network, BitTorrent is delivering an open, efficient, and durable infrastructure for the decentralized AI frontier.

The rollout of these twin initiatives marks BTT’s evolution from a standard utility and governance token into a revenue-backed deflationary asset, underscoring BitTorrent’s steadfast commitment to long-term value creation. Crucially, it launches the BitTorrent ecosystem into a self-reinforcing flywheel of sustainable growth, direct value accrual, and strategic expansion.

Inaugural BTT Buyback & Burn Completed: 100% Decentralized Revenue Powers Deflationary Flywheel

The rollout of this long-term buyback-and-burn program marks BitTorrent’s most decisive step yet to refine its tokenomics and reinforce ecosystem value.

BitTorrent set this long-term roadmap in motion on July 6, introducing a sustainable, revenue-backed deflationary model. Under this framework, 100% of all decentralized business revenue is channeled directly into BTT buybacks and burns, executed systematically across each calendar quarter. Moving past short-term, marketing-driven buybacks financed by outside capital, this structure creates genuine value capture driven purely by real business performance.

In line with this schedule, BitTorrent completed its inaugural buyback using Q3 2026 revenue from its decentralized services. On October 16, a total of 21,621,611,570,729.6 repurchased BTT tokens, valued at approximately $7,600,907, were sent to the black-hole burn address. Trackable via transaction hash 4d9596617780e329bbd4e644ee0dffd780ec4cf3749f324d03eb98157eb04ae5, this irreversible on-chain burn permanently removes the tokens from circulation, providing the market with transparent and verifiable proof of deflation.

To guarantee end-to-end transparency and traceability, BitTorrent has set a rigorous benchmark for on-chain disclosure. Alongside the brand upgrade, a dedicated BTT buyback-and-burn dashboard is now live on its official website. Going forward, burn figures and corresponding on-chain records will be published on this page around the middle of the first month of every subsequent quarter, offering the market a transparent, predictable deflationary schedule.

Market reception has been overwhelmingly positive. Recent trading data shows strong upward momentum, with BTT posting an impressive gain of approximately 30.3% over the trailing three months as of October 15. This rally highlights investor confidence in BitTorrent’s operational cash flow and long-term prospects, confirming that this revenue-driven deflationary model has sparked a powerful engine for BTT’s value growth.

Fueling this long-term deflationary mechanism is BitTorrent’s ambitious expansion into distributed networks, cross-chain interoperability, and AI compute. This widening business footprint creates a fully self-sustaining commercial loop. As utility expands, the buyback initiative ignites a powerful flywheel that bridges revenue generation, token deflation, value distribution, and network growth. Stronger business operations and independent revenue streams provide an ever-growing financial base for BTT buybacks. In return, the rising intrinsic value of the token organically attracts more global nodes and developers, fueling the next massive leap in network adoption.

BitTorrent Reborn: A New Blueprint for Web3 and AI Infrastructure

BitTorrent is rewriting its DNA. Driven by a new whitepaper and a massive tokenomics upgrade, the protocol has officially transcended its legacy boundaries. Now firmly anchored as the definitive infrastructure for Web3 and AI applications, this strategic evolution transforms BitTorrent’s multi-tiered network into a powerhouse of deep, cross-layer synergy and structural vitality. 

The explosive rise of generative AI and Web3 has hit a structural wall: sluggish data delivery, fractured compute power, and punishing on-chain settlement fees. BitTorrent confronts this bottleneck head-on. Under an evolved strategic narrative, the new whitepaper re-engineers BitTorrent’s stack from the ground up, unifying its core capabilities into a cohesive infrastructure. It decisively positions BitTorrent as a comprehensive infrastructure ecosystem spanning content distribution, decentralized compute, and on-chain scaling and settlement, driven by a tripartite synergy uniting the BitTorrent Mainnet, the BTTInferGrid decentralized compute network, and the BTTC scaling network.   

Within this reimagined architecture, individual verticals no longer operate in silos; they function as interlocking gears. BitTorrent Mainnet acts as the ecosystem’s primary gateway and data distribution layer, driving peer-to-peer content delivery to connect global users, nodes, and bandwidth at scale. In tandem, the newly integrated BTTInferGrid powers the decentralized compute layer, matching distributed GPU capacity with active demand to deliver elastic, cost-efficient, and verifiable AI inference for developers and dApps. Bridging these layers, BTTC anchors Layer 2 scaling, cross-chain interoperability, and settlement across networks like TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain. Leveraging EVM compatibility, low gas fees, and high-frequency throughput, it executes service settlements, node staking, reward distributions, and cross-chain payments. Unifying the entire network, the native BTT token serves as the core economic engine, covering critical utilities across resource payments, gas fees, node incentives, staking, and governance.

Uniting distributed content delivery, decentralized compute, on-chain execution, and tokenomics, the reborn BitTorrent stands as an open infrastructure network built for the Web3 and AI frontier. The strategic integration of an AI compute tier decisively drives BitTorrent beyond data routing into high-value intelligent processing and full-stack solutions. Each product line operates as an independent service tier for users and developers while integrating via standardized interfaces and the BTT tokenomic engine. Together, they establish a closed-loop infrastructure pipeline spanning data distribution, compute execution, outcome verification, and on-chain settlement.

Above all, BitTorrent’s next chapter comes down to its community and the builders. The updated whitepaper refines BTT governance, putting real decision-making power and tangible economic rewards directly into the hands of the community. That philosophy comes alive through a 100% decentralized buyback-and-burn model, ensuring that every dollar earned by the network is transparently returned to token holders and ecosystem contributors.

Backing its Web3 and AI evolution with an ongoing BTT buyback-and-burn model marks a defining leap for BitTorrent. It confirms strong profitability and durable business foundations, laying down a direct blueprint to lead decentralized infrastructure. With its value-capture flywheel running at full speed, BitTorrent moves into the future of Web3 and AI with fresh momentum, an open architecture, and lasting staying power.

Over the past year, JUST has completed five consecutive large-scale buyback-and-burn rounds, permanently removing 1.88B JST tokens from circulation and pushing cumulative deflation toward 19%. Following this milestone, the buyback and burn mechanism is set to undergo a comprehensive upgrade.

On October 17, JUST, the leading DeFi infrastructure in the TRON ecosystem, announced the completion of its fifth buyback and burn of its native token JST as scheduled. Over 170M JST were burned in this round (approx. 1.72% of total supply), backed by nearly $23.53M in capital deployed—all funded directly by JustLend DAO’s net operating revenue.

Over the past five rounds, a total of 1.88B JST tokens have been burned, driving the cumulative deflation rate past 19% with over $100M revenue deployed.

JST has reached a key operational milestone following this latest burn: the remaining 70% of JustLend DAO’s initial treasury reserves has been fully deployed according to the original plan. This marks the successful completion of the first phase , paving the way for a major mechanism upgrade.

170M+ Tokens (~$23.53M) Burned in JST’s Fifth Buyback Round

According to the official announcement released, the fifth JST buyback and burn was successfully completed. As a routine buyback for Q3 2026, a total of 170,723,144 JST tokens (approx. 170M) were burned, representing about 1.72% of the total token supply, with a total value exceeding $23.53M.

Maintaining similar levels of burn scale and capital investment to the previous four rounds, this burn round continues the stable, predictable execution cadence of JST buybacks and burns.

Looking further into the source of funds, the funds  invested in this buyback and burn came entirely from JustLend DAO’s net operating income, specifically composed of two parts: the remaining $10.34M from JustLend DAO’s existing income and the $9.28M QoQ increase in Q3’s net income.

In terms of quarterly revenue performance, JustLend DAO’s Q3 net income remained steady compared to previous quarters. With quarterly earnings consistently anchored at the eight-figure ($10M+) level, the ecosystem’s core revenue streams continue to prove their resilience.

At the same time, deploying the remaining 70% of the initial revenue reserve means that the early-stage treasury reserve plan has officially reached its conclusion—setting the stage for a brand-new phase of the buyback program.

One Year, Five Burns: JST’s Price Soars 300% with $100M Deployed from JustLend DAO’s Revenue

From its launch in October 2025 to the fifth round on October 16, 2026, the JST buyback and burn mechanism has completed one full year of operation across five consecutive burn rounds. A total of approximately 1.881B JST tokens have been burned, representing a cumulative deflation rate of > 19% with more than $100M deployed from JustLend’s revenue.

A breakdown of the five buyback and burn executions is as follows:

– Round 1 (October 19, 2025): Burned ~559M JST (~5.66% of total supply), with ~$17.72M deployed.

– Round 2 (January 14, 2026): Burned ~525M JST (~5.3% of total supply), with ~$21M deployed.

– Round 3 (April 15, 2026): Burned ~271M JST (~2.74% of total supply), with ~$21.3M deployed.

– Round 4 (July 17, 2026): Burned a total of ~355M JST (~3.59% of total supply), with ~$34.59M deployed. In addition to the routine quarterly buyback, this round incorporated dedicated burn funds from USDJ’s historical stability fees (~$10.39M) for the first time.

– Round 5 (October 16, 2026): Burned ~170M JST (~1.72% of total supply), with ~$23.53M deployed.

In terms of operational intensity, the execution of five consecutive rounds in a single year—averaging roughly $20M per round, with over $100M committed from real protocol earnings and nearly one-fifth of the total token supply burned—places JST among a select tier of buyback programs rarely seen in the DeFi sector.

This continuous execution has transformed the buyback from a series of short-term news catalysts into a permanent value engine. Rather than acting as an isolated marketing tactic, the program transmits its impact systematically through a five-pillar chain: Capital Foundation—Execution Assurance—Transparency & Trust—Deflationary Scarcity—Market Feedback, cementing a durable foundation for long-term valuation.

On the capital foundation, JST buybacks rely directly on authentic business cash flows. Except for the historical USDJ stability fee allocation in Round 4, every dollar of the $100M+ deployed across all five rounds originated directly from JustLend DAO’s organic operating earnings.

In execution assurance, both capital scale and operational cadence have been uncompromisingly delivered. Single-round commitments began at $17.72M in Round 1, stabilized around $20M thereafter, and reached $34.59M in Round 4. Throughout all five quarters, every burn landed strictly on schedule—free from delays, disruptions, or arbitrary cuts.

For transparency and trust, every buyback follows the standard procedure of “pre-disclosed rules, on-schedule execution, and verifiable on-chain proof”, backed by immutable on-chain transaction records and open official disclosures.

In deflationary impact, around 1.881B JST tokens have been burned across five rounds, contracting total supply from 9.9B down to ~8.02B—a nearly 19% reduction that continuously compounds structural scarcity.

Ultimately, market feedback validates the mechanism through synchronized gains in both token price and market cap. CoinGecko data shows JST climbing steadily from its ~$0.03 low in October 2025 to an October 10 peak of $0.142—a 300%+ year-to-date surge marking a new high since 2022—while circulating market cap surged past $1B.

This closed-loop flywheel—fueled by authentic revenue, reliable execution, complete transparency, structural deflation, and market validation—has elevated the buyback program far beyond short-term hype, solidifying it as the central pillar sustaining JST’s long-term economic value.

Buyback Mechanism Poised for Comprehensive Upgrade as Capital Sources Diversify

 With five consecutive rounds now complete, the JST buyback program arrives at a watershed moment: the first phase officially concludes, setting the stage for a new upgraded phase.

Looking back at the initial phase, the framework was initially structured to draw backing jointly from JustLend DAO and USDD. Under the original terms, USDD’s cross-chain ecosystem revenue was to feed into the buyback pool once cumulative earnings hit $10M—a threshold not yet reached. Consequently,  this early phase operated primarily on JustLend DAO’s accumulated treasury reserves alongside the increment in quarterly net revenue. Specifically, the $59M+ reserve earmarked at inception under the plan of “30% upfront, 70% in phased tranches” has now been fully deployed across five rounds. This signifies that the initial phase has smoothly achieved its objectives, clearing the path for  the comprehensive upgrade.

As outlined in the JST Q1 2026 financial report released in April, the upgraded JST buyback  mechanism will broaden capital sources beyond the existing framework by incorporating revenues from new business streams such as GasFree, providing deeper and more diversified funding for ongoing buybacks.

With the upgraded phase around the corner, JST’s long-term deflationary momentum and value-return capabilities are poised to enter an even more sustainable and predictable cycle. For specific plans regarding capital allocation, execution cadence, and ecosystem integrations under this upgraded mechanism, follow JUST’s official X account @JUST_DAO for the latest updates.

Washington, D.C., October 18, 2026 — The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA), a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing clear and ethical public policy, research, and education related to emerging technologies, participated in Nacha’s Payments Innovation Alliance Fall Meeting, where DSA Senior Policy Advisor Molly Woodman joined industry leaders to discuss emerging technologies, regulatory developments, and the future of domestic and global payments.

Held October 14-16 at the InterContinental Chicago Magnificent Mile in Chicago, Illinois, the three-day meeting brought together stakeholders from across the financial services and payments industries to exchange insights, address operational challenges, and explore opportunities for innovation. Discussions focused on evolving payment technologies, regulatory considerations, and practical approaches to navigating an increasingly complex financial landscape.

As part of the Alliance’s ongoing initiatives, Woodman facilitated discussions surrounding the newly launched Next-Gen Currency Project Team, a project co-led by Nacha and DSA. The team explores the global use of digital assets, including stablecoins and tokenized deposits, for money movement. Its work focuses on developing tools to bridge digital assets and traditional payment systems, tracking regulatory developments, identifying operational implications, and providing educational resources to the payments industry.

Throughout the meeting, participants also examined practical challenges facing financial institutions as emerging technologies reshape payment systems. Topics included expectations for financial institutions regarding agentic payments, the reliability of multifactor authentication methods as technology evolves, and emerging approaches to Know Your Agent (KYA) frameworks. Discussions highlighted the importance of industry collaboration in addressing operational uncertainties and developing workable solutions as regulatory frameworks continue to evolve.

“It’s been encouraging to watch financial institutions brainstorm together on how to build some continuity in areas where regulation hasn’t caught up yet,” said Molly Woodman, Senior Policy Advisor at DSA.

DSA’s participation reflects its ongoing commitment to supporting informed policy discussions and collaboration across the financial services and emerging technology sectors. Through its involvement in the Next-Gen Currency Project Team and broader industry engagement, DSA works to advance approaches that support responsible innovation, regulatory clarity, and the integration of emerging technologies into the evolving payments landscape.

The Digital Sovereignty Alliance (DSA) is a nonprofit social welfare organization committed to advocating for public policies that support ethical innovation in decentralized technologies, blockchain, cryptocurrency, Web3, and artificial intelligence. HONG KONG, October 18, 2026 – As quantum computing advances, the challenge extends beyond Bitcoin’s cryptography to the financial infrastructure built around it.

Quantum computing is emerging as one of Bitcoin’s long-term security challenges. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could theoretically compromise the digital signatures protecting Bitcoin transactions, potentially exposing funds associated with vulnerable public keys.

While no publicly demonstrated quantum computer is currently capable of such an attack at scale, the implications extend beyond Bitcoin itself. As Bitcoin becomes increasingly integrated into decentralized finance (DeFi) through tokenized assets such as Wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC), a future cryptographic transition would affect not only the Bitcoin network, but also the financial infrastructure built around it.

The question is no longer simply whether Bitcoin can become quantum-resistant, but whether the broader ecosystem can evolve alongside it.

Beyond the Bitcoin Network

Bitcoin’s transition to quantum-resistant cryptography would require more than introducing new signature schemes. Wallets, exchanges, custodians and infrastructure providers would need to adapt their systems, potentially migrating existing BTC holdings to new security standards.

Proposals such as BIP-360 reflect ongoing efforts to explore Bitcoin’s future cryptographic architecture. Yet coordinating adoption across a decentralized ecosystem could take years.

For tokenized Bitcoin, the challenge becomes more complex. Even if Bitcoin adopts quantum-resistant cryptography, the custody systems, smart contracts and networks supporting tokenized assets would still require independent security assessments.

Securing Bitcoin itself does not automatically secure everything built around it.

WBTC and the Next Generation of Bitcoin Infrastructure

As an established tokenized Bitcoin asset in DeFi, WBTC illustrates the scale and complexity of securing Bitcoin across multiple financial ecosystems.

With 116,000 WBTC in circulation, representing approximately $9.5 billion in Bitcoin-backed assets, WBTC’s infrastructure supports Bitcoin liquidity across lending protocols, decentralized exchanges and multiple blockchain networks.

Backed 1:1 by BTC held in custody, WBTC’s long-term resilience depends not only on Bitcoin’s underlying cryptography, but also on reserve security, custody operations and the infrastructure supporting minting and redemption.

A future quantum-resistant transition could require custodians to evaluate their key-management systems, migrate underlying BTC reserves and maintain operational continuity throughout the process.

Against this backdrop, WBTC is preparing to migrate to new Custodian Bitcoin Deposit Addresses (CBDAs) as part of its custody infrastructure management. Bitcoin address management is relevant to long-term security because public-key exposure can influence vulnerability to potential quantum attacks. However, the security implications depend on address types and transaction histories, and address migration alone does not establish quantum resistance.

WBTC has also publicly announced its exploration of a multi-custodian reserve model, aimed at reducing custody concentration risk and strengthening operational resilience. While diversification does not directly address quantum vulnerabilities, it could provide greater flexibility as security standards evolve, depending on implementation.

Together, these initiatives highlight the importance of both reserve security and operational resilience as Bitcoin’s financial ecosystem expands. Neither replaces the need for quantum-resistant cryptography, but both illustrate the infrastructure considerations involved in preparing for future changes.

Preparing for the Next Era

The timeline for quantum computing remains uncertain, but preparing for potential cryptographic changes is a long-term challenge for the entire Bitcoin ecosystem.

For WBTC, this means considering how custody arrangements, reserve management and supporting blockchain infrastructure could evolve alongside Bitcoin’s security standards.

Bitcoin’s quantum transition may begin with cryptography, but its success will depend on the resilience of the infrastructure connecting Bitcoin to the wider financial ecosystem.

About WBTC – Bitcoin’s Passport to DEFI
WBTC is the new Bitcoin standard. A singular identity for Bitcoin across multiple chains. It brings Bitcoin into environments where speed, capital efficiency, and scale are essential, while maintaining fidelity to Bitcoin’s original principles. There is no second. WBTC stands alone in its role, trusted, verifiable, and engineered for a multichain world.

title: Wall Street freaked out Friday, but VIX and bitcoin trades say the fear may fade Monday.
summary: Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX index, spiked on Friday as stocks dropped. History says Friday panics usually fade on Monday. Seasonality and calm bitcoin markets suggest the same.
content:
Updated Oct 18, 2026, 7:24 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 18, 2026, 12:33 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Wall Street’s fear gauge, VIX, surged 21.5% Friday as stocks fell. Traders are betting the fear index will stay elevated through November.
  • Historical data suggests Friday VIX spikes typically ease on Monday.
  • Bitcoin remains above $80,000 over the weekend, with its own fear gauge, BVIV, pinned in familiar ranges, showing no signs of market stress.

Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX index, ripped higher on Friday as stocks tanked on AI and geopolitical worries. Bitcoin BTC$82,001.05 traded in a choppy manner as well.

Traders are betting the fear gauge keeps climbing.

However, if VIX history and bitcoin’s steady weekend price action are any guide, the panic could subside just as quickly on Monday.

First, a quick primer. Cboe’s VIX measures how much traders expect the S&P 500, the blue-chip stock index, to swing over the next four weeks. It's derived from options prices. When people get nervous, they buy options, which are contracts used to hedge against price swings. That pushes the VIX up.

Bitcoin BTC$82,001.05, meanwhile, is the only macro asset thats trades over the weekend. As such, swings in bitcoin over the weekend are often seen as lead indicators of how traditional markets may open on Monday.

Friday’s VIX surge

On Friday, the VIX jumped 21.5% to 19.99 as the S&P 500 fell by 1.09%.

That's VIX’s biggest one-day rise since June 5, when the S&P 500 suffered its worst day in months, according to data source TradingView.

Traders are betting the VIX stays high through November. CNBC reports that traders bought 9,200 of the Nov. 18, 20-strike calls for $1.7 million. Traders also bought 12,500 of the Nov. 18, 23-strike calls for $1.1 million. The bet is that the VIX closes above 23 by the third week of November.

That sentiment is consistent with the present macro developments. AI stocks have been hit hard in the week gone by. The cost of default insurance on AI-related firms has hit record highs. Geopolitics is pushing oil higher too. On Saturday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The Russia-Ukraine front looks like it's heating up as well.

VIX history favors a Monday reset

Big Friday jumps in the VIX usually don't last, according to historical data.

CoinDesk's analysis of the data finds the VIX has jumped 20% or more on a Friday 32 times since January 1990, not counting the latest one. The next Monday, it fell 25 times and rose just seven.

In other words, investors slept over the Friday panic over the weekend and things normalized on Monday. The typical Monday move was a drop of 4.5%. A month later, the VIX was lower in 25 of the 32 cases, and the median drop was 16%.

Seasonality also favors the VIX bears, and by extension stock market stability.

The VIX has declined in November in 25 of the last 36 years, with a median drop of 7.2%. From October end to the end of the year, VIX has fallen in 22 of 36 years, with a median decline of 9.4%.

Bitcoin remains above $80,000

Bitcoin isn’t flinching. It continues to trade above $80,000, comfortably within its recent choppy range, suggesting Friday’s risk aversion and VIX rise may not carry into Monday.

The bitcoin market has been more active over the weekend this year, especially on Sunday, as geopolitical flareups that began in early March keep investors on edge. That activity highlights bitcoin’s role as a always-on macro asset: When traditional markets are shut, traders use bitcoin to express their early read on global risk appetite.

Volmex's BVIV, the bitcoin volatility index, or the bitcoin VIX, slipped 1% on Friday to just under 40% and has barely moved since. BVIV shows the 30-day implied or expected volatility in bitcoin.

Bettors on the decentralized platform Polymarket aren't panicking either. They see just an 9% chance the AI bubble bursts this year as of this writing.

Past doesn’t guarantee future results

None of the above guarantees a stable Monday. Moreover, in seven of the 32 cases, the VIX kept climbing sharply on Monday, including in August 2015, February 2018 and August 2024.

Going purely by the VIX levels, there's room for the index to run.

Even after Friday’s spike, the VIX is still under 20, a mark it has topped on more than a third of days since 1990. It has closed above 30 on just 8% of days. So, if fear grips the market further on Monday morning, the VIX can climb.

title: Bitcoin Price Faces 10 Big Tests as 5 Catalysts Keep $100K Alive
summary: Bitcoin’s bulls are still talking six figures while the market struggles to hold $81,000. With ten potential market movers approaching and five catalysts capable of reviving momentum, the coming week could settle some arguments. Bitcoin’s price enters Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, in a peculiar predicament...
content:
Bitcoin’s bulls are still talking six figures while the market struggles to hold $81,000. With ten potential market movers approaching and five catalysts capable of reviving momentum, the coming week could settle some arguments.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin traded near $81,000 on Oct. 18 after losing roughly 1.3% to 2.2% over seven days.
  • Five potential catalysts could help bitcoin reclaim $100,000, including stronger ETF inflows.
  • Bitcoin faces 10 market tests during Oct. 19-25, with $80,000 support remaining critical.

Bitcoin’s price enters Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, in a peculiar predicament. The cryptocurrency has spent another week fighting to preserve its footing above $80,000, yet some influential market commentators have been proclaiming the arrival of another bull market this month. The enthusiasm looks rather ambitious against a backdrop of stubborn inflation, institutional fund withdrawals and repeated failures to reclaim $84,000. Still, the optimists have a case worth examining. Moreover, five potential catalysts could eventually carry bitcoin back above $100,000, while ten developments during the coming week threaten to determine whether the market finds its second wind or takes another beating.

Bitcoin’s Rough Week Leaves Bulls Behind the Eight Ball

Bitcoin declined approximately 1.3% to 2.2% over the past seven days, retreating from the $83,700 to $84,000 neighborhood toward $81,000 by Sunday morning. The leading crypto asset tapped an intraday low of $80,888 on Bitstamp at 11:15 a.m. Eastern time.

The trouble began Oct. 12, when BTC slipped toward $81,000 before recovering above $83,000 the following day. That comeback proved short-lived. September’s U.S. consumer price index (CPI), reported at 3.7% annually in the supplied figures, renewed inflation concerns and helped push bitcoin toward $79,700 to $80,200 on Oct. 15. By Sunday, BTC had recovered to approximately $81,950 to $82,100, gaining 0.5% to 0.7% over 24 hours. Trading volume hovered around $13 billion to $15 billion, consistent with comparatively subdued weekend participation.

Resistance remains concentrated between $83,000 and $84,000, while buyers have defended the $80,000 to $81,000 neighborhood. The daily relative strength index (RSI), around 48 to 49, suggests neither side has established convincing control.

Meanwhile, U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) experienced approximately $617 million in October net withdrawals through midmonth. Institutional demand, once the market’s favorite ace in the hole, is facing another test.

10 Developments That Could Shake Bitcoin Next Week

The Oct. 19-25 calendar contains enough economic releases and market developments to keep traders on their toes. Some are scheduled events, while others depend on how institutional investors and leveraged speculators respond.

No.Market catalystWhat traders should watch
1China’s economic report, Oct. 19Third-quarter GDP, industrial production and retail sales will offer clues about global growth. Weak figures could pressure bitcoin and other risk assets.
2U.S. housing figures, Oct. 20Housing starts and building permits will test economic resilience amid elevated borrowing costs, potentially influencing Treasury yields and Fed expectations.
3Weekly jobless claims, Oct. 22Expectations near 200,000 claims leave room for surprises that could shift interest rate forecasts and cryptocurrency sentiment.
4Global business activity, Oct. 23Preliminary PMIs from major economies will reveal manufacturing and services conditions, with weak readings potentially dampening risk appetite.
5Spot bitcoin ETF flowsOctober’s reported $617 million in net withdrawals has rattled institutional confidence. Renewed inflows could help restore buying momentum.
6Bitcoin’s technical battlegroundSupport at $80,000 to $81,000 remains crucial. Reclaiming $83,000 to $84,000 could reopen the road toward $86,000 to $87,000.
7Futures funding and open interestPositive funding indicates leveraged bullish positioning. Rising open interest alongside falling prices could intensify liquidation pressure.
8Approaching Fed meetingThe Fed’s communications blackout ahead of Oct. 27-28 puts economic releases in the spotlight as traders reassess interest rate expectations.
9Stocks, oil and geopoliticsNasdaq performance, energy prices and Treasury yields could influence bitcoin as investors weigh economic and geopolitical uncertainty.
10Corporate buying and onchain activityStrategy’s accumulation, exchange balances and large-holder transfers could reveal whether investors are absorbing supply or preparing to sell.

Five Catalysts That Could Put $100,000 Back on the Table

Despite the gloomy technical picture, bitcoin needs an advance of approximately 22% from $82,000 to reclaim six figures. Five potential developments could help deliver that move.

No.Bullish catalystHow it could push bitcoin toward $100,000
1Revival in institutional ETF demandU.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have attracted more than $56 billion in cumulative net inflows since January 2024. Sustained weekly inflows of $500 million to $1 billion could strengthen demand and tighten available supply.
2A friendlier Federal ReserveCooling inflation, falling Treasury yields and potential interest rate cuts could improve liquidity conditions, encouraging investors to return to bitcoin and other risk assets.
3Greater regulatory clarityConstructive SEC and CFTC guidance on cryptocurrency custody and trading could remove institutional barriers, opening the door to greater participation from banks, financial advisers and investment firms.
4Corporate treasury accumulationStrategy reportedly holds approximately 848,250 BTC, more than 4% of bitcoin’s eventual supply. Continued corporate acquisitions could intensify competition for available coins and strengthen buying pressure.
5Expanded Treasury liquidity supportLarger U.S. Treasury bond buybacks and easing long-term yields could improve financial conditions while reinforcing bitcoin’s appeal as a potential hedge against fiscal deficits, government debt and monetary debasement.

None guarantees a six-figure bitcoin price. Several working together, however, could substantially improve the market’s prospects.

Bull Market Predictions Meet an Uncomfortable Reality

Interestingly, some cryptocurrency influencers have declared that another bull market is beginning despite October’s lackluster performance. The supplied material does not identify those commentators or provide their statements, leaving the claims unverified.

“Congratulations, the bull market is here,” the X account Crypto Rover wrote last week. “Brace yourself. You’re about to become the first crypto millionaire in your family,” the account added. Two days later, another X account stated:

“This bitcoin signal NEVER fails. Most people feared another crash when the Death Cross flashed. In reality, it has historically marked major BTC cycle bottoms. I called the EXACT bottom using this signal. The bull market is HERE, and ignoring it could be your most expensive mistake.”

The contradiction is nevertheless striking. Bitcoin remains roughly 35% below its October 2025 record near $126,200, institutional flows have weakened, and buyers haven’t convincingly reclaimed nearby resistance. For the bulls, the immediate assignment is straightforward. Defend $80,000, recover $84,000 and demonstrate that institutional demand is returning.

For the bears, another rejection could keep bitcoin trapped in its correction, potentially opening the door to considerably lower prices. The market has heard plenty of predictions about $100,000. This week, it gets another chance to see whether the money agrees.

title: Latvia eyes crypto tax payments in 2027 as parliament overhauls crypto taxation
summary: Parliament passed a law taxing crypto withdrawals above deposits rather than individual trades, featuring a one-time declaration mechanism.
content:
Summary

  • Latvia plans to allow residents to pay personal taxes with cryptocurrency as early as next year, according to PM adviser Didzis Dejus.
  • Parliament passed a law taxing crypto withdrawals above deposits rather than individual trades, featuring a one-time declaration mechanism.
  • The initiative aims to attract crypto firms and investors, supporting asset tokenization and positioning Latvia as a fast-moving fintech hub.

Latvia could allow residents to pay personal taxes with cryptocurrency as early as next year, as part of a push to attract crypto firms and investors.

The country’s Finance Ministry has agreed to the plan, though technical work with a payment provider remains, said Didzis Dejus, an adviser to the prime minister on strategic planning and the new economy.

Asked whether Latvians would be able to pay taxes in crypto during the prime minister’s term, Dejus told CoinDesk at the UN:BLOCK Fintech conference in Riga that “I believe that will take place next year.”

CoinDesk has reached out to Latvia’s Finance Ministry for comment but hasn’t heard back at the time of writing.

The move would give crypto holders a way to use their assets to meet tax bills. It also builds on plans announced in May 2025 to enable crypto tax payments and the tokenization of other assets like real estate.

“We are not afraid to be the fastest country,” Dejus said, describing efforts to attract crypto business beyond licensing.

The proposal comes as Latvia changes how it taxes crypto investments. On Oct. 15, the country’s parliament passed legislation to tax withdrawals from crypto investment accounts once they exceed the amount deposited, rather than taxing each trade.

The law also introduces a one-time declaration process. Holders can settle past tax obligations by paying 10% of their declared assets’ market value at the end of 2026. Declarations can be filed from April 1 to May 31, 2027, with the tax due by July 23.

Dejus said the measure would help people who bought crypto years ago but lack records to prove what they paid.

The payment plan’s timing could depend on the next government. Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs’ United List won the Oct. 3 parliamentary election, and is expected to be renominated, but still needs coalition partners.

Latvia would not be the first government to accept crypto for taxes. Colorado started allowing crypto tax payments through PayPal in 2022, with funds converted into dollars.

Dejus did not name Latvia’s payment provider or say which cryptocurrencies would qualify to pay taxes.

title: Qubic Loses $1.3 Million in Wallet Raid Before Network Halts
summary: An overnight cryptocurrency theft emptied 1,404 Qubic wallets of approximately 2.94 trillion QU, worth $1.3 million, before validators halted the network. The apparent culprit wasn’t a blockchain vulnerability but predictable wallet seeds generated by older Apple devices and browsers. With most stol...
content:
An overnight cryptocurrency theft emptied 1,404 Qubic wallets of approximately 2.94 trillion QU, worth $1.3 million, before validators halted the network. The apparent culprit wasn’t a blockchain vulnerability but predictable wallet seeds generated by older Apple devices and browsers. With most stolen tokens trapped on the paused network and another portion frozen by MEXC, the fate of victims’ funds now rests with Qubic’s validators.

Key Takeaways

  • Qubic reported 1,404 wallets drained of approximately 2.94 trillion QU between Oct. 17 and 18.
  • Qubic attributed the theft to predictable wallet seeds generated by older Apple software.
  • MEXC reportedly froze the stolen tokens it received, while Qubic’s quorum considers restitution.

Qubic Exploit Drains 1,404 Wallets as Network Freezes $1.3 Million Theft

A cryptocurrency thief managed to empty 1,404 Qubic wallets in less than two hours, stealing roughly 2.94 trillion QU worth $1.3 million without hacking the blockchain itself. Instead, the attacker apparently exploited something far simpler: predictable wallet recovery seeds generated by older software. By the time Qubic’s validators intervened early Sunday, Oct. 18, most of the stolen funds were still on the network, while an exchange had frozen another portion, leaving an extraordinary digital heist effectively trapped in place.

Predictable Wallet Seeds Opened the Door

Qubic reported that the unauthorized transfers occurred between 23:42 UTC Saturday and 01:26 UTC Sunday. Computors, the network’s validators, subsequently halted transactions at tick 85,371,949. The vulnerability involved insufficient randomness when generating 55-character wallet seeds. Rather than guessing an astronomical number of possible combinations, the attacker apparently reconstructed a smaller collection of predictable seeds and identified wallets holding funds.

Affected wallets included seeds generated on iPhones and iPads through browsers, Macs running Safari, and older versions of Qubic’s iOS application. Developers said the issue was corrected in version 4.26.4. They also secured additional vulnerable funds before the attacker reached them. Qubic’s native currency is down more than 10% at 10 a.m. Eastern time on Sunday morning.

Most Stolen Tokens Remain Frozen

The attack’s aftermath produced an unexpected complication for the thief. Approximately 87.1% of the stolen QU remained on Qubic, immobilized by the network suspension. The remaining 12.9% reportedly reached cryptocurrency exchange MEXC, which froze the receiving account. QEARN stakes were reportedly unaffected. Bitget subsequently suspended QUBIC deposits and withdrawals for maintenance. Whether victims receive reimbursement now depends on decisions by Qubic’s Computor quorum.

A Network With a Controversial History

Qubic was founded by Sergey Ivancheglo, also known as “Come-from-Beyond,” an early blockchain developer associated with NXT and IOTA. The project attracted controversy in 2025 after claiming majority control of Monero’s mining hashrate, followed by blockchain reorganizations that alarmed the privacy coin’s community.

This time, Qubic wasn’t challenging another network’s security. It was confronting a weakness in its own wallet software, with billions of tokens immobilized and victims awaiting a decision on restitution.

title: Stablecoin supply stalls, but payments jump 45% as Visa, Mastercard and Stripe connect crypto to cash
summary: Analytics firm Allium said stablecoin payments hit $482 billion this year so far, up 45%, as card spending surges and global payment firms add crypto rails.
content:
Oct 18, 2026, 10:00 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Stablecoin payments grew 45% to $482 billion this year through September, despite circulating supply stalling in 2026, according to a fresh report by blockchain analytics firm Allium.
  • Mastercard, Stripe and Visa all announced services this week that combine stablecoins with familiar payment systems as digital dollars become increasingly part of global money movement.
  • Businesses want stablecoins being integrated into their existing financial operations, instead of running separate systems for digital assets, said CEO of Paris-based enterprise payments firm Fipto.

Stablecoin supply has barely budged this year, but the digital dollars already in circulation are doing more work in payments, according to a fresh report from blockchain analytics firm Allium.

Stablecoin payments are growing at a rapid pace, reaching $482 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 45% from a year earlier, the report found.

That growth contrasts with the broader stablecoin market. The total value of stablecoins — cryptocurrencies tied to fiat currencies such as the U.S. dollar — in circulation stood at about $305 billion at the end of September, up a meager 0.4% since the start of the year, according to the report.

The number of payments grew even more, jumping 71% to over 1 billion, the report said, suggesting that stablecoins are changing hands more often without much new supply entering the market.

Stablecoin-linked cards showed some of the fastest growth. Spending measured by Allium reached $3.9 billion through September, ten times the amount a year earlier. Small purchases — under $50 — accounted for 84% of the increase in card transactions.

Stablecoins meet traditional payment rails

Three announcements earlier this week offered a glimpse of how stablecoins are becoming increasingly part of global payments.

Mastercard (MA) introduced Thursday its Global Money Platform with BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure firm it acquired in August. The service combines traditional currency accounts, stablecoin balances, conversions, card spending and bank payouts through one connection.

Banks and fintechs can use the platform to offer accounts that hold both fiat currencies and stablecoins, the firm said. Payments firms Nuvei and Marqeta are among the first customers integrating that service.

Stripe, meanwhile, is working with Plasma XPL$0.07875, a blockchain-based financial services firm, on cards that support balances in dollars, euros, Brazilian reais, Mexican pesos and Colombian pesos, alongside eligible stablecoins.

The companies said they plan to let customers spend from the balance that matches their purchase, cutting unnecessary currency conversions. Stripe's expanded card infrastructure covers more than 30 countries, with plans to reach over 100 by next year.

Read more: Stripe to expand stablecoin cards to over 100 countries by the end of the year

And Visa (V) said it is bringing stablecoins into the funding side of international payments.

The company said Inyo Global, a payment orchestration firm for fintech, money transmitter, banks, became the first provider to put Visa Direct's stablecoin prefunding service into commercial use. Payment firms can use Circle's (CRCL) dollar stablecoin USDC USDC$1.0003 to fund cross-border payouts in nearly real-time instead of waiting for traditional banking windows, while recipients can still receive money through conventional payment channels.

A small slice of a vast payments market

That rapid growth of stablecoin payments comes with some caveats. Of $97.9 trillion in raw stablecoin transfers through September, Allium classified just $2.4 trillion, or 2.5%, as end-user activity after filtering out exchange, decentralized finance and automated transactions. Its $482 billion payments estimate comes from that smaller pool, the report said.

Stablecoin cards also remain a tiny fraction of conventional payments. Allium estimated that second-quarter spending through those cards amounted to just 0.03% of Visa's $4 trillion in payment volume.

For payment companies, that leaves a large market to pursue. Nuvei CEO Phil Fayer, whose company is among the first to integrate Mastercard's new platform, said stablecoins are becoming part of how businesses move money across borders and currencies.

"The future of global commerce depends on money moving as freely as the businesses and consumers it serves, across borders, currencies and increasingly, between traditional and digital forms of money," Fayer said.

The recent efforts by Mastercard, Stripe and Visa to incorporate stablecoins on blockchain rails reinforce that trend. Companies increasingly want stablecoins integrated into their existing financial operations, instead of running separate systems for digital assets, according to Patrick Mollard, co-founder and CEO of Paris-based Fipto, a stablecoin-powered business payments firm.

“The distinction between 'traditional' and 'digital' money is less important than giving businesses the ability to use whichever rail makes most sense for a particular payment or treasury operation,” he said in a note shared with CoinDesk.

“Businesses don't want separate crypto infrastructure sitting alongside their existing financial operations,” Mollard said. “They want to move between fiat and stablecoins within the same payments and treasury environment.”

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, AIsa said it had completed its seed extension round with Tether and HIVEN joining as strategic investors, stablecoin issuer Circle is seeking to enter about 40 developing markets, according to CEO Jeremy Allaire, and a new report highlighted substantial cost savings from stablecoin remittances, especially in emerging markets.

Tether backs AIsa as strategic investor, completing seed extension round

AIsa said it had completed its seed extension round, with Tether and HIVEN joining as strategic investors.

The round brings AIsa’s total funding to more than $9 million. The two new investors joined Alibaba, Tribe Capital, Sumitomo Corporation, Draper Associates, Saison Capital and other backers.

“Enterprise AI agents need trusted information, useful tools and a governed way to transact,” said Jordan Liu, founder and CEO of San Francisco-based AIsa, in a Friday statement. “Our vision is to build the infrastructure that enables agents to discover, access and pay for resources globally, while giving enterprises full control over permissions, spending and transactions. We are excited to welcome Tether and HIVEN as strategic investors as we accelerate the transition from AI assistants to autonomous, production-ready agents.”

Fragmented providers, integrations and billing systems make it difficult for enterprise AI agents to operate effectively in production and manage at scale, according to the statement.

AIsa addresses this by bringing resource discovery, access and transactions into one governed, usage-based network, the Trusted Resource and Transaction Network for Enterprise AI Agents. Its infrastructure connects enterprise agents to external data, AI search, models, APIs, software tools and industry services, combining governed access with usage metering, billing and settlement, the
statement said.

Circle’s Allaire says stablecoin issuer looking to enter 40 developing markets: Report

Stablecoin issuer Circle is seeking to enter about 40 developing markets, according to the company’s CEO and ​chairman, Jeremy Allaire.

“We’re kind of going through an inflection point...a transition right now, ‌and that transition is essentially moving from the early adopter phase of blockchain technology into the mainstream scaling phase,” Allaire told Reuters, speaking Friday on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank meetings ​in Bangkok.

Markets in Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East are experiencing increasing demand for stablecoins as businesses and individuals seek to enter the internet-based economic system, Allaire reportedly said. 

Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, Borderless finds

Stablecoin-funded remittances cost roughly 84% less than traditional money transfers, according to a new third-quarter report from payments network Borderless.xyz.

Sending $200 through stablecoin payment networks costs a median of $2, or 1%, compared with $12.72, or 6.36%, for conventional remittances. The comparison uses Borderless pricing from the third quarter of 2026 and World Bank data from the same period last year.

Savings were particularly pronounced in emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the respective costs were 1.25% and 5.64%.

Businesses also stand to benefit. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26, compared with $135 to $150 for an international bank wire, including foreign-exchange costs.

Stablecoin payouts also settled faster in several markets, with a median of two minutes in Brazil and Colombia and three minutes in Mexico. Traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day.

However, reliability varied. Payment completion rates reached 98.6% in Mexico but fell to 73% in Costa Rica, highlighting differences in local payment infrastructure.

title: Most Americans polled oppose betting on elections: Reuters
summary: The prediction market industry enables people to bet on US ‌elections and sporting events.
content:
Most Americans polled by Reuters/Ipsos are opposed to betting on US elections and other government actions.

The prediction market industry, led by Polymarket and Kalshi, enables people to bet on US ‌elections, government policy moves and sporting events, which has resulted in a series of lawsuits involving state and federal agencies over who has the authority to regulate these markets.

Some 69% of Democrats ​and 61% of Republicans polled said they opposed using prediction markets to bet on election results. The Reuters/Ipsos survey of 4,506 adults nationwide was taken on Sept. 30-Oct. 5.

Related: Blockchain.com pursues CFTC approval for prediction markets: CNBC

Even betting ⁠on professional sports was opposed by 43% of respondents, while 29% supported it, the poll said.

President ​Donald Trump’s administration is pursuing federal regulations for the industry through the CFTC, some of which are begin challenged in court by several states. Many expect ​the dispute to reach the US Supreme ⁠Court.

Cointelegraph reported on Oct. 8 that 39 states and the District of Columbia filed an amicus brief in a New Jersey case contending the conflict between the CFTC and state authorities over prediction markets had resulted in a “national turf war” that could not be resolved without an answer from the Supreme Court.

Assets: BTC

Bitcoin’s latest wave of loss-selling near $80,000 may indicate that selling pressure is approaching exhaustion, according to on-chain data from Glassnode.

Similar spikes in Bitcoin’s realized losses preceded local price bottoms in August and September, raising the possibility that the $80,000 region could provide near-term support for BTC.

However, the Bitcoin price outlook remains uncertain. Technical resistance near $83,000, continued spot Bitcoin ETF outflows, and concentrated liquidation levels around $80,600 and $82,300 suggest that BTC could face further volatility before establishing a clearer direction.

Glassnode Identifies Signs of Seller Capitulation

Glassnode reported another episode of Bitcoin seller capitulation on October 15, 2026, as BTC traded near the $80,000 region. Capitulation occurs when investors sell their holdings at a loss, often during periods of heightened uncertainty or declining prices.

Glassnode reports renewed Bitcoin seller capitulation on October 15, with realized loss spikes coinciding with local price bottoms in August and September 2026. Source: Glassnode via X

In its October 16 report, Glassnode noted that previous bursts of realized losses in early August, mid-August, and September coincided with local market bottoms. The latest episode follows a similar pattern, although the historical relationship does not guarantee another recovery.

Realized losses measure the value investors give up when they sell Bitcoin below the price at which they acquired it. A sharp increase in this metric can indicate that holders are exiting positions under pressure rather than waiting for a rebound.

Glassnode’s latest analysis also points to a decline in loss-taking among long-term holders. In its October 14 report, Boxed In, the analytics firm said long-term holder realized losses had fallen approximately 85% from their August 12 peak. The report also noted that holders realizing profits were increasingly outweighing those selling at a loss.

These developments provide a potentially constructive signal for the BTC price. When forced or emotionally driven selling subsides, the market may require less immediate buying demand to stabilize. Nevertheless, capitulation alone cannot confirm that a durable bottom has formed.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: $80K Support Faces a Critical Test

Bitcoin was trading around $82,000–$83,000 in the October 15–16 reporting period after briefly falling below $80,000 earlier in the month. The recovery places BTC above the psychologically important $80,000 level, but the market still needs to overcome nearby resistance.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Glassnode identified the U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF cost basis near $81,500 as an important support reference. This represents the average acquisition price of Bitcoin held by U.S. spot ETFs. According to the firm’s October 14 analysis, BTC dipped below this level on October 8 and October 13 but closed both sessions above it.

The firm warned that a daily close below the ETF cost basis could weaken the nearest on-chain support. Its report also identified substantial bids around $80,000 on Binance, creating another level to watch if selling pressure returns.

Meanwhile, a separate technical analysis published on TradingView by Virupandey81 identifies $79,821 as a key downside threshold. The chart places the initial positional-long reference at $81,263 and calls for confirmation before adding exposure above $83,014.

Bitcoin climbed from around $75,000 to $87,000 before correcting, recovering toward its previous high, and declining again, forming overlapping harmonic patterns. Source: Virupandey81 on TradingView

If Bitcoin holds above support and clears the $83,014 confirmation level, the chart identifies $87,233 as the first upside objective, followed by a projected extension near $91,754. These are technical targets rather than confirmed forecasts, and reaching them would require BTC to overcome intervening resistance.

A sustained move below $79,821 would weaken that bullish setup. The same chart identifies lower projected levels near $77,839 and $76,377, which could become relevant if the breakdown continues. Neither level guarantees a reversal.

The distinction is important for any Bitcoin price prediction: a potential support zone becomes more convincing when price repeatedly holds above it, while a decisive breakdown can invalidate an otherwise constructive setup.

Bitcoin Liquidation Heatmap Highlights $82.3K and $80.6K

Bitcoin’s derivatives market provides another indication of where short-term volatility could develop. CoinGlass shared a 48-hour liquidation heatmap showing concentrated leveraged positions around $82,300 and $80,600.

Bitcoin’s 48-hour liquidation heatmap shows concentrated high-leverage liquidation clusters around $82,300 and $80,600. Source: CoinGlass via X 

The upper zone near $82,300 represents a nearby cluster of potential liquidations, while the lower region around $80,600 contains another concentration of leveraged exposure. As BTC approaches these levels, forced position closures could amplify price movements.

Liquidation heatmaps estimate where leveraged positions may be vulnerable to forced closure. They do not show guaranteed buying or selling orders, and the displayed clusters can change as traders adjust their positions.

A move above $82,300 could trigger liquidations among traders positioned for further declines, potentially adding momentum to an upward move. Conversely, a drop toward $80,600 could put leveraged long positions under pressure, increasing the risk of a faster decline.

These levels also sit close to the broader support region highlighted by Glassnode. Their proximity makes the $80,000–$82,300 range particularly relevant to the near-term Bitcoin price forecast.

However, liquidation activity should be assessed alongside spot-market demand, trading volume and ETF flows. A temporary price spike caused by forced closures does not necessarily establish a lasting trend.

Bitcoin ETF Outflows Add Pressure to the Price Outlook

Despite the potential support signals from on-chain data, institutional investment flows remain a concern. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $228.6 million in net outflows during the five trading sessions ending October 16, according to reported fund-flow data. Month-to-date net outflows reached roughly $615 million to $618 million.

BlackRock reportedly sold $570 million in Bitcoin as bearish forecasts warned of a potential drop to $75,000 after a brief rebound. Source: @Danny_Crypton via X

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for approximately $165 million in weekly outflows, including about $71.8 million on October 16. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund also recorded outflows during the period.

These figures indicate that investors withdrew more money from the funds than they added during the measured period. However, they do not establish that BlackRock independently sold $570 million in Bitcoin on the open market, as claimed in a post by @Danny_Crypton on X.

ETF outflows reflect net investor redemptions and fund activity; they should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that an asset manager is deliberately pushing Bitcoin prices lower. The distinction matters when evaluating claims about institutional selling and the risk of a Bitcoin crash.

Continued redemptions could still weaken a source of market demand, particularly if they coincide with broader risk aversion. Glassnode’s October 14 report similarly noted that spot Bitcoin ETFs had returned to net selling after inflows in late September failed to persist.

The combination of ETF outflows and declining realized losses presents a mixed picture. Selling pressure among existing holders may be easing, but fresh investment demand has not yet provided a clear signal of sustained recovery.

What Comes Next for Bitcoin Price?

Bitcoin’s next move will likely depend on whether buyers can defend the $80,000 region while absorbing selling pressure and overcoming nearby resistance.

The bullish scenario gains support if BTC maintains the area around the $81,500 ETF cost basis, holds above the $80,000–$80,600 support zone, and moves through $83,014. Under the TradingView chart’s projections, $87,233 would be the first upside target, with $91,754 representing a more distant objective.

The bearish scenario becomes more relevant if Bitcoin loses the $79,821 technical threshold and fails to recover it. In that case, the projected levels around $77,839 and $76,377 would become areas to monitor, while liquidation activity could accelerate the decline.

Glassnode’s capitulation data offers evidence that some selling pressure may be reaching an extreme, but it is only one part of the market picture. ETF flows, liquidity conditions, spot demand, and price behavior around support will help determine whether the latest loss-selling episode marks a local floor or merely another pause in Bitcoin’s decline.

For now, the $80,000 region remains a key reference point in the Bitcoin price prediction. A sustained recovery would strengthen the case for higher targets, while a decisive breakdown would challenge the emerging stabilization signal.

title: Bitcoin’s $100,000 year-end hope divides analysts as inflation clouds outlook
summary: Bitwise sees a potential return above $100,000, while LO:TECH expects a narrower trading range as interest-rate uncertainty weighs on the market.
content:
Oct 18, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • Bitwise sees bitcoin potentially topping $100,000 by year-end, supported by institutional adoption and demand for hard assets.
  • LO:TECH expects an $85,000–$95,000 year-end range as inflation and rate-hike risks constrain gains.
  • Laser Digital sees potential for a short squeeze, while CoinShares says a sustained breakout needs renewed buying.

Bitcoin BTC$82,001.05 could reclaim $100,000 before year-end as institutional adoption and demand for hard assets overcome near-term economic uncertainty, according to crypto asset manager Bitwise, offering a more bullish outlook than traders who expect inflation and elevated interest rates to constrain gains.

The forecasts highlight a divide over timing. Analysts see longer-term support from institutional investment, regulatory progress and concerns about government debt, but disagree on whether those forces can drive a breakout before the end of 2026.

Ryan Rasmussen, head of research at Bitwise, expects bitcoin to emerge from the coming weeks’ uncertainty at a higher valuation.

“We believe bitcoin ends the year higher, potentially above $100,000,” Rasmussen told CoinDesk.

He identified three longer-term drivers: institutional buying through exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and corporate purchases; demand for hard assets amid inflation, rising debt and currency debasement; and clearer regulation that reduces the perceived risk of owning crypto.

“In our view, these tailwinds significantly outweigh the potential headwinds,” he said.

The macro hurdle

Rasmussen nevertheless expects volatility around a possible late-October Federal Reserve rate increase and November’s U.S. midterm elections. A breakout would be difficult in that environment, he said, although the uncertainty could create an opportunity for investors to build positions.

Adam Morgan McCarthy, head of research at LO:TECH, a London-based crypto trading and market data firm, is more cautious. His base case is an $85,000–$95,000 trading range into year-end.

“Macro has gone against Bitcoin all year, with the Fed hiking in September and a December hike priced at roughly 75%,” McCarthy said. “This will continue to weigh on bitcoin.”

The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point in September. Inflation figures released Oct. 14 complicated the outlook: consumer prices rose 0.6% from the previous month, while core prices increased 0.3%. Gasoline accounted for more than half of the headline increase.

McCarthy said a return above $100,000 would require expectations for a December hike to give way to a pause, supported by easing oil prices and inflation.

James Butterfill, head of research at CoinShares, sees a similar tension between persistent inflation and weakening employment. Cooling prices would give the Fed more room to respond to labor-market weakness; further inflation pressure could keep policy restrictive and weigh on bitcoin.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency was trading around $81,500 at publication time.

Less leverage, potential for a squeeze

Luca Invernizzi, senior derivatives trader at Laser Digital, Nomura’s crypto subsidiary, expects bitcoin to remain largely a macro trade into year-end, taking its direction from longer-dated Treasury yields.

He described the rebound from summer lows as unconvincing, citing thin volumes, fading ETF inflows and slowing corporate buying.

Positioning offers more encouragement. Leverage has largely been flushed out of bitcoin, with much of the speculative excess moving into altcoins, Invernizzi said.

McCarthy also sees fewer crowded bullish positions that could unravel. Funding rates, payments between perpetual futures traders, are at or below zero, while August’s rally was driven by traders closing bearish bets rather than adding new bullish positions.

That reduces the fuel for forced selling and leaves room for another squeeze higher.

“A clean break above $90K for BTC could trigger another round of short covering,” Invernizzi said.

With implied volatility back near its lows and options pricing still tilted toward downside protection, he sees upside calls as an attractive way to position for a rally without chasing bitcoin in the spot market.

Longer-term demand

The broader industry’s recovery provides another source of optimism.

In a research note to clients earlier this week authored by Peter Christiansen, Citi (C) said total crypto market capitalization rose from roughly $2.1 trillion to nearly $3 trillion during the third quarter. Institutional ETF flows turned positive, while activity across exchanges, stablecoins and digital asset infrastructure improved.

The bank also sees investors increasingly looking beyond crypto prices toward businesses supporting tokenization, custody, stablecoins and settlement. Regulatory progress continues despite the Clarity Act’s failure to advance, Citi said.

Butterfill cautioned that investment-product flows have since slowed following $11.1 billion of inflows since mid-July. He views that as uncertainty rather than deteriorating bitcoin fundamentals, but said sustained gains require renewed buying.

Like Rasmussen, he sees concerns about government finances as a potential longer-term source of demand. Higher Treasury yields typically hurt bitcoin by tightening financial conditions, but that relationship could shift if investors increasingly interpret those yields as compensation for fiscal risk.

“Our bias is towards higher prices over the medium term, but we would want to see the fiscal argument translate into sustained allocations before expecting a decisive breakout,” Butterfill said.

Rasmussen is more confident those forces will translate into gains sooner.

“Once the market churns through this period, we expect bitcoin to rerate significantly higher,” he said.

title: Crypto audits give investors false sense of security as Q3 hacks cost $1.18 billion, Hacken says
summary: The security firm found that 77% of third-quarter losses involved compromised suppliers, delayed fixes or systems outside the latest security reviews.
content:
Oct 18, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Hackers stole $1.18 billion from crypto projects in the third quarter, up 55% from the previous quarter, according to blockchain security firm Hacken.
  • About $900 million in losses stemmed from compromised suppliers or developer tools, uninstalled security fixes or components excluded from security reviews.
  • Hacken warned that audit badges can give investors a false sense of security because reviews often omit wallets, signing systems and third-party software that attackers target.

Crypto investors may be putting too much faith in security audits that fail to cover the systems hackers actually target, according to blockchain security firm Hacken.

In a report released on Thursday, Hacken found that hackers stole $1.18 billion across 107 incidents during the third quarter, 55% more than in the previous quarter. Of that amount, $906.8 million was lost due to compromised suppliers or developer tools, publicly available security fixes that were not installed or components excluded from the most recent security review.

"The problem is always scope." Andrii Matiukhin, co-founder and board director at the company, said in an interview with CoinDesk. "It's expensive to have enormous scopes of all components that interact with funds or influence economics, and teams cut corners, auditing only critical parts of the service.”

The findings raise questions about how much protection investors can expect from crypto projects advertising themselves as audited. Hacken said customers often assume an audit covers an entire platform when it may examine only specific smart contracts, leaving wallets, signing systems and third-party software outside its scope.

“Usually, when a customer sees a new project, they see an audit badge, assume the whole system is covered, and lose money through a key, a supplier, or a setting that was never tested,” Matiukhin said.

The biggest incident in the period was the September attack on crypto exchange Bitget, which lost at least $352 million after hackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product to gain access to its withdrawal infrastructure, according to the report.

The risks extend beyond exchanges. Just this week, hardware wallet maker Ledger said it found an unauthorized hardware “spy” implant in a device sold by CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller, resulting in losses of about $93 million.

Three crypto bridges and cross-chain protocols lost more than $35 million during a six-hour exploit in July, Hacken said. AFX Trade accounted for $24 million of that after attackers gained control of its validator keys. Other attacks walked off with $319 million at Liquid Network, at least $75 million at Tectonic, and roughly $114 million at Coldcard wallet software.

Hacken also examined 12 derivatives exchanges and prediction markets and found that more than $700 million in secure assets at two major venues depended on a four-key signing arrangement requiring three signatures, or on administrative keys whose holders were not publicly identified.

Matiukhin declined to identify the venues or provide a detailed assessment before publication of the report. He said it had found no evidence of an active vulnerability, but considered some of the arrangements inadequate given the amounts involved.

“We are not aware of a live bug in the systems of any reviewed venue,” Matiukhin said. “Instead, what we found is setups where key setups are not secure enough considering the scale of the venues reviewed.”

Matiukhin said delays in fixing known vulnerabilities were another concern, particularly when multiple blockchains relied on the same software but updated it at different times.

“Sometimes a critical vulnerability is classified as low by the team, and fix implementation is delayed or even declined,” Matiukhin said.

Responsibility ultimately rests with the companies holding customer funds, which must track vulnerabilities and install fixes promptly rather than rely on an audit completed months or years earlier, Hacken said.

title: Hedera (HBAR) Price Analysis as Long-Term Compression Tests Support
summary: The price of Hedera (HBAR) is returning to $0.08275, a major technical support level, amid bearish pressure.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: HBAR

The price of Hedera (HBAR) is returning to $0.08275, a major technical support level, amid bearish pressure.

The monthly chart of the instrument has a long-term pattern of a triangle, which may form the next significant price action. On the 4-hour time frame, HBAR has broken above its October highs, signaling a momentum decline.

The major issue is whether buyers can justify the existing support level and hold the market. If the sustained recovery continues, the resistance could be seen in the descent, and if the breakdown occurs, the lower levels near $0.071 could be seen.

HBAR Faces Selling Pressure Below $0.092

According to BraveNewCoin market data, HBAR is currently trading at $0.08275, falling by 2.61% in the last 24 hours. The token’s price range in the past 24 hours is 0.08207-0.08710. The value of its market capitalization is $3.64 billion, and the trading volume is $104.75 million.

On the other hand, the 4-hour chart for HBAR indicates that the token is currently trading at $0.08234 on October 17, 2026. The price is out of the trendline chart and sitting near $0.09212. with a falling trendline. This is now the level that is an upper limit for recovery, but buyers need to muster a powerful response to test it.

Four-Hour Chart Signals Further Downside Risk

On the 4-hour chart, HBAR is consolidating its gains and heading back to the $0.12 level from its highs seen in late September. The ongoing sell-off has driven the token near the bottom of its Bollinger Bands. The bottom of its lower band is at $0.07103, and the top of its upper band is at $0.11322.

HBAR is trading at $0.09212, which is close to the middle line of the chart’s trend indicator. Source: TradingView

This formation indicates that the sellers are still holding the upper hand in the recent price trend. But a turn up from below $0.09212 would be better for the near term and could create resistance at $0.10.

Monthly Triangle Keeps the $0.57 Level in Focus

HBAR continues to trade inside of a long-term triangle pattern, as seen on the monthly chart shared on X. Both rising support and descending resistance continue to the lows from 2020 and 2021 highs, respectively. The price has been compressed between these two trending lines over the past few years, hence the pattern.

The chart below shows a possible scenario for a breakout where HBAR may move back toward $0.57 in the future. Source: Giannis Via X

This level corresponds to the peak from the provided market data that occurred in the past. However, this is a conditional projection, and the price hasn’t confirmed a breakout above the descending resistance.

Support and Resistance Levels to Watch

The immediate support level is around $0.0820, the daily low for HBAR. If the price stays below this level for an extended period, it may reach the lower Bollinger Band around $0.07103. Traders can also watch to see whether buyers support the wider uptrend on the monthly chart.

The good news is that HBAR will need to rally to $0.09212 to threaten its downtrending near-term condition. Further resistance could emerge around $0.10 and the recent peak above $0.12. A close-out above the monthly triangle’s resistance would support the big-time recovery outlook.
